title: Lookup in a concatenation over a range
statement: Let $k,n$ be natural numbers and let $f$ assign a list to each natural number, with $f(z)$ of length $k$ whenever $z<n$. For $z<n$, $r<k$, and a default element $d$, the entry at position $zk+r$ in the concatenation of $f(0),\ldots,f(n-1)$, with default $d$, equals the entry at position $r$ in $f(z)$, with the same default.
hypotheses_covered: A list-valued function $f$ on the natural numbers
For each $z<n$, the list $f(z)$ has length $k$
A default element $d$ of the list type
